issues.description: can_form_k_palindrome incorrectly updates digit frequencies when placing a digit in a non-middle palindrome position. The backtracking consumes only one occurrence (remaining_freq[digit] -= 1) even though placing a digit at a non-middle position uses two copies (left and right), so the routine can build palindromes from impossible frequency distributions and produce wrong results.

Inconsistent mapping between position index and powers-of-ten exponents. The code treats pos==0 as the most-significant digit for the purpose of rejecting leading zeros, but uses pow10_mod_k[pos] (which is 10^pos, the least-significant exponent) when adding the contribution; this mismatch makes the numeral construction incorrect and leads to wrong divisibility checks and improper leading-zero enforcement.

The approach enumerates all n-digit numbers via recursive construction with a complex frequency tuple state. For n up to 10 this state space may grow very large and could be inefficient / prone to TLE in worst-case inputs. Consider a combinatorial / DP by frequency or arithmetic construction to reduce complexity.

No test files were delivered with the submission (no unit tests or sample-case checks). The Definition of Done includes fixing the failing case from the previous run; add automated tests (at least the provided examples and edge cases) to validate the correction.
